item.title: The Taiwan Affairs Office of Jiangxi Launches National Defense Education Activity to Carry Forward the Long March Spirit
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-13
The Taiwan Affairs Office of Jiangxi Launches National Defense Education Activity to Carry Forward the Long March Spirit Source: Taiwan.cnUpdated: 2026-10-13
Oct 13(Taiwan.cn)—Recently, the Taiwan Affairs Office of the CPC Jiangxi Provincial Committee organized all Party members and cadres of the office to visit the Jiangxi Provincial Museum for a national defense education activity. The group toured the exhibitions The Great Departure, the Eternal Long March: Exhibition on the History of the Central Red Army’s Departure for the Long March and Red Cradle: Exhibition of Jiangxi Revolutionary History. The activity aimed to guide cadres and staff in studying revolutionary traditions and enhancing their awareness of national defense. During the visit, the participants followed in the footsteps of history. They deeply reflected on the firm convictions and fearless sacrifice of revolutionary predecessors, as well as their arduous journey marked by perseverance and courage in overcoming hardships. The activity helped them gain a deep understanding of the paramount importance of national defense and national security, offering profound ideological refinement and spiritual edification. After the visit and study, Party members and cadres stated that the tour was both an in-depth education in revolutionary history and a vivid lesson in national defense. As cadres engaged in Taiwan-related work in the new era, they will inherit and carry forward the great Long March Spirit, uphold the glorious traditions and fine conduct of Communists, firmly embrace the holistic approach to national security, and continuously strengthen their awareness of national defense and potential risks. They will translate their insights into concrete actions to tackle challenges and deliver results. In line with their duties, they will deepen cross-strait exchanges and cooperation across various fields in Jiangxi. With high morale and pragmatic measures, they will promote high-quality development of Taiwan-related work in the province, actively foster spiritual affinity between compatriots on both sides of the Taiwan Strait, contribute to writing the Jiangxi chapter of Chinese modernization, and advance the great cause of national reunification.(Jointly reported by Taiwan.cn and the Taiwan Affairs Office of Jiangxi) Related Stories

item.title: Taiwan Affairs Office of Yuwangtai District, Kaifeng City Launches Taiwan-Related Publicity and Education Campaign in Enterprises
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-13
Oct 13(Taiwan.cn)—On October 10, the Taiwan Affairs Office of Yuwangtai District, Kaifeng City, held an event to bring Taiwan-related publicity and education into enterprises. Representatives of local entrepreneurs gathered to study policies related to Taiwan affairs, discuss hot policy topics and ideas for industrial and commercial development, talk about cross-Strait integrated development, and express their patriotism and devotion to their home and country. During the event, the person in charge of the Taiwan Affairs Office of Yuwangtai District led participants in studying the overall strategy of the Communist Party of China (CPC) for resolving the Taiwan question in the new era. Drawing on the historical origins, cultural ties, and current developments across the Taiwan Strait, the official elaborated on the profound blood bond and shared destiny between compatriots on both sides of the Strait. The official also expounded on the core essence and spiritual connotations of the white paper The Taiwan Question and China’s Reunification in the New Era. The activity guided participants to accurately grasp the overall trend of cross-Strait relations and fully understand the historical and legal basis for Taiwan being an inalienable part of China’s territory. It also encouraged local entrepreneurs to actively explore practical ways to promote the message that “both sides of the Taiwan Strait are one family” in economic and trade exchanges and interactions, contributing to the deepening of cross-Strait integrated development. Representatives of enterprises at the event said that the activity served as a systematic study of policies and theories, a vivid lesson in patriotism and love for the homeland, and a heart-to-heart exchange that built consensus. Going forward, enterprises will draw on their actual operations and industrial strengths to actively identify entry points and areas of focus for linking their sectors with cross-Strait exchanges. They will proactively act as advocates and liaisons for cross-Strait exchanges, carry forward the kinship rooted in the shared origins of people across the Strait in daily business operations and external interactions, and build stronger momentum for cross-Strait integrated development. (Jointly reported by Taiwan.cn and the Taiwan Affairs Office of Kaifeng)

item.title: 22nd Guangxi-Taiwan Economic, Trade and Cultural Cooperation Forum to Be Held in Nanning, Guangxi, in October
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-13
22nd Guangxi-Taiwan Economic, Trade and Cultural Cooperation Forum to Be Held in Nanning, Guangxi, in October Source: Taiwan.cnUpdated: 2026-10-13
Oct 13(Taiwan.cn)—In the golden autumn of Yongcheng (Nanning), Guangxi and Taiwan will write a new chapter in cooperation. The 22nd Guangxi-Taiwan Economic, Trade and Cultural Cooperation Forum is scheduled to take place in Nanning, Guangxi, from October 19 to 21, 2026. With the theme “Empowering a New Era through Digital Intelligence, Forging a Future via Guangxi-Taiwan Integrated Development,” the forum will be co-hosted by the People’s Government of Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region and the Taiwan Affairs Office of the State Council. The forum will be held at a time when the Pinglu Canal has been officially completed and opened to navigation, and a series of events commemorating the 160th anniversary of Dr. Sun Yat-sen’s birth are underway. The full opening of the Pinglu Canal has turned the century-old vision of river-sea transportation laid out in Dr. Sun Yat-sen’s The International Development of China—connecting rivers to the sea and enabling integrated river-ocean shipping—from a blueprint into reality. Currently, Guangxi is accelerating the development of ten modern pillar industries. Following a path of digitalization, green development, and integration, it is leveraging artificial intelligence as a core driver to advance industrial transformation and upgrading. Meanwhile, Guangxi has rolled out systematic measures for its marine economy, ushering in a new phase of building strength through marine development and pursuing opening-up and growth. These development opportunities not only open up broad new space for Guangxi’s high-quality development but also inject strong momentum into exchanges and cooperation between Guangxi and Taiwan. The forum will feature an opening plenary session and two parallel thematic sub-forums: “Development Paths and Practices of Artificial Intelligence in Guangxi and Taiwan” and “Building a New Ecosystem for the Guangxi-Taiwan Marine Economy through River-Sea Coordination.” Taking digital and intelligent industries as the link and the Pinglu Canal as an open platform, participants from Guangxi and Taiwan will conduct in-depth exchanges and discussions on key areas of cooperation, including electronic information technology, artificial intelligence, port logistics, and marine fisheries, jointly exploring new paths for mutually beneficial cooperation. (Jointly reported by Taiwan.cn and the Taiwan Affairs Office of Guangxi) Related Stories

item.title: Mainland slams Lai Ching-te's secessionist narrative
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-12
Mainland slams Lai Ching-te's secessionist narrative BEIJING, Oct. 10 (Xinhua) -- A Chinese mainland spokesperson on Saturday criticized Taiwan leader Lai Ching-te for clinging to a secessionist mindset, provoking confrontation, and undermining peace and stability across the Taiwan Strait. Zhang Han, spokesperson for the State Council Taiwan Affairs Office, made the remarks in response to a media question about Lai's speech delivered in Taipei earlier in the day. Lai's speech disregarded facts, distorted right and wrong, misled the public and harbored ulterior motives, Zhang said, describing it as a typical display of his self-proclaimed stance as a "pragmatic worker for Taiwan independence." In his speech, Lai played up the so-called mainland threat and promoted the false narrative of "democracy versus authoritarianism," Zhang said. Lai was attempting to pursue "Taiwan independence" through military buildup and reliance on external forces, the spokesperson added. The Taiwan question stems from a full-blown civil war fought between the forces led by the Communist Party of China (CPC) and the Chinese Kuomintang (KMT) about eight decades ago. In 1949, the remnants of the defeated KMT retreated to Taiwan, and the People's Republic of China was founded under the leadership of the CPC. The unresolved civil war and foreign interference have left the two sides of the Strait in a prolonged state of political confrontation, but the fact that Taiwan is an inalienable part of China's territory has never changed. The one-China principle is a basic norm governing international relations, a prevailing consensus in the international community, and an integral part of the post-World War II international order, Zhang said. "The future of Taiwan must be decided jointly by all Chinese people, including Taiwan compatriots," the spokesperson said. The mainland will uphold the one-China principle and the 1992 Consensus, work with people from all sectors of society in Taiwan, resolutely combat secessionist forces, and oppose external interference, Zhang said. The mainland will also deepen cross-Strait exchanges and cooperation, and promote the peaceful and integrated development of cross-Strait relations, she noted.

item.title: Xinhua Commentary: Taiwan leader's repackaged rhetoric cannot conceal his secessionist agenda
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-12
Xinhua Commentary: Taiwan leader's repackaged rhetoric cannot conceal his secessionist agenda BEIJING, Oct. 10 (Xinhua) -- Taiwan leader Lai Ching-te reiterated his secessionist agenda and stoked cross-Strait tensions in a speech in Taipei on Saturday, using carefully crafted rhetoric to mislead the Taiwan public and sway international opinion. Once again, he invoked "democracy" to sensationalize the so-called "mainland threat" and promote a false narrative of "democracy versus authoritarianism." Such rhetoric seeks to exploit the concept of democracy to justify secessionism. The Taiwan question originated from a civil war fought between the forces led by the Communist Party of China (CPC) and the Kuomintang (KMT) about eight decades ago. In 1949, the defeated KMT retreated to Taiwan, while the People's Republic of China was founded under the leadership of the CPC. The unresolved civil war and foreign interference have left the two sides of the Taiwan Strait in a prolonged state of political confrontation. However, the fact that Taiwan is an inalienable part of China's territory has never changed. Both history and reality make clear that Taiwan's future should be jointly decided by all Chinese people, including Taiwan compatriots. Differences in political systems are neither an obstacle to China's reunification nor an excuse for splitting the country. Lai said he would "never allow the distortion of World War II history." Yet his own words have repeatedly distorted history and undermined the outcomes of WWII. Lai refused to say a word about China's victory in the War of Resistance Against Japanese Aggression and the historical fact that Taiwan was restored to China after being freed from Japan's colonial rule. Instead, he has used the term "the end of the war," favored by Japanese right-wing forces, in place of references to Japan's defeat in the war. Lai's speech also contained statements that stoked confrontation across the Strait rather than promoting reconciliation. He pledged to continue military reforms, strengthen asymmetric warfare capabilities and increase military spending, while claiming that these measures were intended to deter war rather than provoke it. But such rhetoric cannot conceal his true colors as a saboteur of peace, a maker of crises and an instigator of war. The worsening of cross-Strait relations since the secessionist-minded Democratic Progressive Party came to power in 2016 demonstrates that secessionist moves in pursuit of "Taiwan independence" pose the greatest threat to peace and stability across the Strait. Since taking office, Lai has established a so-called Whole-of-Society Defense Resilience Committee, constantly conducted military exercises and civil-military integrated drills, designated numerous civilian facilities as purported wartime response centers, expanded military spending, and stepped up arms purchases from external sources. These moves have heightened cross-Strait tensions and exposed Taiwan to greater security risks. Lai's stubborn adherence to secessionism runs counter to the Taiwan people's aspirations for peace, development, and cross-Strait exchanges and cooperation. It also disregards the broader interests of the Chinese nation. No matter how he repackages his rhetoric or disguises his intentions, the secessionist agenda behind his words remains evident. Reunification is an inevitable historical trend. Attempts to pursue "Taiwan independence," including through military means, lead nowhere. People on both sides of the Taiwan Strait share fundamental interests in peace, stability and development. People in Taiwan should join their fellow Chinese on the mainland in opposing secessionism, upholding peace and stability across the Strait, and advancing the cause of national reunification.

item.title: Mainland experts say Taiwan leader's speech shows separatist agenda unchanged, undiminished
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-12
Mainland experts say Taiwan leader's speech shows separatist agenda unchanged, undiminished BEIJING, Oct. 11 (Xinhua) -- Mainland Taiwan affairs experts said the speech delivered on Saturday by Taiwan leader Lai Ching-te in Taipei is filled with deception, noting that his refined rhetoric cannot conceal his push for separatism. Chen Guiqing, a research fellow at the Beijing-based Institute of Taiwan Studies, Chinese Academy of Social Sciences, said that Lai paid lip service to peace and cross-Strait exchanges, while repeatedly attacking and vilifying the mainland, groundlessly accusing it of applying pressure through military and "gray zone" actions and of attempting to alter the status quo in the Taiwan Strait. "The remarks fully expose Lai's stubborn separatist mindset and his intention to incite confrontation across the Strait," Chen added. Chen pointed out that facts have repeatedly shown Lai and the Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) authorities as the source of undermining cross-strait stability and social harmony in Taiwan. "Lai's speech skirted the economic and social challenges facing Taiwan," Chen said. "The remarks were apparently designed to serve the DPP's interests in the upcoming local elections." The Taiwan question originated from a civil war fought between the forces led by the Communist Party of China (CPC) and the Kuomintang (KMT) about eight decades ago. In 1949, the defeated KMT retreated to Taiwan, while the People's Republic of China was founded under the leadership of the CPC. The unresolved civil war and foreign interference have left both sides of the Taiwan Strait in a prolonged state of political confrontation. However, the fact that Taiwan is an inalienable part of China's territory has never changed. Both history and reality make clear that Taiwan's future should be jointly decided by all Chinese people, including Taiwan compatriots. Differences in political systems are neither an obstacle to China's reunification nor an excuse for splitting the country. Liu Xiangping, an expert on Taiwan studies at Nanjing University, said Lai's hyping of "whole-of-society defense resilience" is essentially a pretext for increasing the island's defense budget and a way to rationalize dragging Taiwan residents onto his separatist chariot. "Lavishing the people's hard-earned money on military expansion at the expense of their livelihoods will ultimately backfire," Liu said. Liu criticized Lai's attempt to curry favor with the United States and the West. "By parroting Western ideological rhetoric, Lai has fully exposed his eagerness to act as a pawn for external forces," the expert said. Lai said he would "never allow the distortion of World War II history." Yet his own words have repeatedly distorted history, said Wang Yingjin, director of the cross-Strait relations research center of the Renmin University of China. Wang noted that on the 80th anniversary of Taiwan's restoration to China, Lai sided with the Japanese invaders by describing the victory in the War of Resistance against Japanese Aggression as merely the "end of the war," which itself distorts the history of WWII.

item.title: Taiwan leader's speech exposes him as threat to peace: mainland defense spokesperson
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-12
Taiwan leader's speech exposes him as threat to peace: mainland defense spokesperson BEIJING, Oct. 11 (Xinhua) -- Taiwan leader Lai Ching-te's recent speech has once again exposed his true colors as a source of trouble for Taiwan and a threat to peace, said a Chinese defense spokesperson on Sunday. Chen Xi, a spokesperson for China's Ministry of National Defense, made the remarks when asked to comment on the speech delivered by Lai in Taiwan on Saturday, in which the Taiwan leader reiterated his secessionist agenda and stoked cross-Strait tensions. Chen noted that in recent years, the Democratic Progressive Party authorities have pursued separatism and rejected reunification for their own party interests, undermining stability in the Taiwan Strait and sacrificing the island's future. The Chinese People's Liberation Army's regular drills and training activities around the island are carried out to deter separatist activities seeking "Taiwan independence" and plots of external interference, and to safeguard the security and well-being of Taiwan compatriots, the spokesperson said. "We hope Taiwan compatriots will join the mainland in combating separatist forces, opposing external interference, safeguarding peace, and sharing the fruits of national rejuvenation," Chen added. The Taiwan question originated from a civil war fought between the forces led by the Communist Party of China (CPC) and the Kuomintang (KMT) about eight decades ago. In 1949, the defeated KMT retreated to Taiwan, while the People's Republic of China was founded under the leadership of the CPC. The unresolved civil war and foreign interference have left the two sides of the Taiwan Strait in a prolonged state of political confrontation. However, the fact that Taiwan is an inalienable part of China's territory has never changed.

item.title: Lai condemned for inciting confrontation
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-12
Lai condemned for inciting confrontation Chinese mainland officials condemned Taiwan leader Lai Ching-te for playing up the so-called "mainland military threat" and inciting confrontation across the Taiwan Strait, saying that his speech on Saturday reflected a separatist mindset and sought to mislead the public. Zhang Han, a spokeswoman for the State Council Taiwan Affairs Office, said that Lai's speech disregarded facts and distorted the truth, exposing his ulterior motives of pursuing "Taiwan independence". Zhang criticized Lai for stubbornly clinging to a separatist "Taiwan independence" mindset and playing up the so-called "mainland threat". She also accused him of promoting the false narrative of "democracy versus authoritarianism" and seeking "Taiwan independence" through force and by relying on external forces. Such moves, Zhang said, stoke confrontation across the Taiwan Strait and undermine peace and stability in the region. "There is only one China in the world, and Taiwan is part of China," Zhang said, stressing that this remains the real status quo across the Taiwan Strait. She added that the one-China principle is a basic norm governing international relations, a broad consensus in the international community and an important part of the post-World War II international order. In his speech in Taipei on Saturday, Lai accused the mainland of "using military actions to pressure Taiwan" and claimed that raising "defense" spending is "not a provocation but a way to deter war". On Sunday, Chen Xi, a spokesman for the Ministry of National Defense, said that Lai's attempts to seek "Taiwan independence" through force and reliance on external forces reflected his nature as a "troublemaker for Taiwan" and a "source of disaster for peace". Chen said that Taiwan's Democratic Progressive Party authorities, for their own party interests, have pursued a separatist agenda and opposed reunification, while currying favor with external forces and seeking their support. He also criticized the DPP authorities for promoting the so-called "whole-of-society mobilization", turning the island into a battlefield, and tying Taiwan people to the "Taiwan independence" agenda. In response to Lai's claims of a so-called "mainland military threat", Chen said the Chinese People's Liberation Army's regular exercises and training around Taiwan are intended to deter separatist moves and external interference, and to safeguard the safety and well-being of Taiwan residents. Bao Chengke, a researcher at a Shanghai cross-Strait studies association, said that Lai's pursuit of "Taiwan independence" is a provocation itself. He said that Lai has increased "defense" spending by using taxpayers' hard-earned money to serve his separatist agenda. Taiwan's proposed "defense" budget for 2027 has increased to NT$1.12 trillion ($35.1 billion), more than double the amount when Lai took office in 2024 and close to 4 percent of the island's GDP, Bao said. "Such an extreme pursuit of military buildup will ultimately harm Taiwan residents and the island's economy," he added. Bao said that Lai is aware that there is little room for pursuing "Taiwan independence" in the international community, and therefore concealed such advocacy while accusing the mainland of "authoritarian expansion". "His remarks are aimed to create a smokescreen for the DPP's pursuit of 'Taiwan independence' separatism," Bao added. Lai also portrayed Taiwan as "a city upon a hill", while pledging to improve social welfare. Critics said he was misleading the public by glossing over social problems and failing to address the real challenges facing Taiwan society. Huang Kuo-chang, chairman of the Taiwan People's Party, expressed his disappointment with Lai's hollow slogans. He said that Lai failed to see the realities faced by people at the foot of the hill, including the widening wealth gap and the plight of traditional industries on the island. Han Kuo-yu, head of the island's legislative body, pointed to fractures in Taiwan's political system during the DPP's tenure. He described last year's mass recall campaign targeting opposition lawmakers, initiated by the DPP, as "a political witch hunt", warning that confrontation between the island's executive and legislative branches would take a toll on people's livelihoods. The recall campaign by the DPP sought to oust opposition lawmakers, but ultimately failed to unseat them. Bao said Lai used the illusory image to mislead Taiwan residents. He pointed out that the DPP authorities have pursued an aggressive military buildup and increased arms spending while neglecting the livelihood and development needs of Taiwan residents, particularly low-income groups. "Social fairness and equality are being eroded by Lai's authoritarianism and intimidation," he added.

item.title: Chinese mainland spokesperson slams Lai Ching-te's flattering remarks on Japan
item.description:
Published: 2026-02-11
Chinese mainland spokesperson slams Lai Ching-te's flattering remarks on Japan Source: XinhuaUpdated: 2026-02-11
BEIJING, Feb. 11 (Xinhua) -- A Chinese mainland spokesperson on Wednesday denounced Taiwan authorities led by Lai Ching-te for ignoring the heinous crimes committed by Japan during its colonial rule over Taiwan, describing their flattering remarks toward Japan as utterly disgraceful. Zhu Fenglian, spokesperson for the State Council Taiwan Affairs Office, made the remarks in response to a media inquiry about Lai's intention to work with Japan to "deal with regional challenges." Zhu also urged the Japanese side to retract Sanae Takaichi's erroneous remarks on Taiwan, handle Taiwan-related issues prudently, and abide by the one-China principle with concrete actions. item.title: Taiwan's DPP authorities slammed for obstructing cross-Strait exchanges
item.description:
Published: 2026-02-11
Taiwan's DPP authorities slammed for obstructing cross-Strait exchanges BEIJING, Feb. 11 (Xinhua) -- A Chinese mainland spokesperson has condemned Taiwan's Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) authorities for imposing restrictions and obstacles on cross-Strait exchanges in pursuit of their "Taiwan independence" agenda and selfish gains. The DPP authorities, led by Lai Ching-te, are the biggest obstacle to cross-Strait interactions and their acts have drawn strong criticism from various sectors in Taiwan, Zhu Fenglian, a spokesperson for the State Council Taiwan Affairs Office, said at a regular press briefing on Wednesday. Zhu expressed the hope that Taiwan compatriots will firmly oppose the retrogressive actions of the DPP authorities and promote exchanges and cooperation across the Taiwan Strait in various fields. She noted that cross-Strait flight routes have been disrupted due to interference from the DPP authorities, with previously operated destinations yet to resume normal operations. In 2025, the average passenger load factor on cross-Strait routes reached 80 percent, reflecting the strong need for direct flights between the two sides of the Strait, Zhu said. "We hope that the Taiwan side will heed public opinion and lift unreasonable restrictions on cross-Strait air transport as soon as possible," she added.
